title: Unified Error Handling & Structured Logging Middleware
description: Introduce a global error‑handling middleware that captures synchronous and asynchronous errors, normalises them into a consistent JSON format, and logs them with structured context. This reduces duplicated try/catch blocks, improves observability, and provides clients with clear error responses.
testCases: When a route throws a standard Error, the response status is 500 and the JSON body contains { code: "INTERNAL_ERROR", message: <error.message> }. The logger records an entry with level "error" and the stack trace.

When a route throws a custom HttpError (e.g., new HttpError(404, "NOT_FOUND", "Resource missing")), the response status matches the error code and the JSON body mirrors the error properties. No stack trace is logged for client errors (4xx).
acceptance: All existing tests pass. New tests verify both generic and custom error flows, confirm response shape, status codes, and that logger is called with appropriate severity and payload. The middleware integrates seamlessly with the existing router without breaking static file serving or other middleware.
reason: Consistent error responses and centralized logging are essential for production stability and debugging. This feature eliminates repetitive error handling code, provides developers with actionable logs, and aligns yantraverse with industry best practices for API frameworks.
